answer: Each apprentice is bound to a master shipwright for seven years, and the guild writes the name, the master and the day in the indenture roll. A wander apprentice claimed as bound fails the roll: the boy must have stood before the guild at the walnut of his binding, and an apprentice never bound has no master to vouch for him. Forging an indenture means bribing the guild clerk, faking a decade of rolls and paying 16,400, and the bridge roll is read at every freedom day, so a man whose binding was never entered builds no ship of his own.
